newsitem.title: GERMANY: Telekom float a success - Deutsche funds unit.
newsitem.headline: Telekom float a success - Deutsche funds unit.

text.p: Deutsche Bank's funds unit DWS said on Thursday it had received seven million shares from last Monday's issue of Deutsche Telekom shares, which amounts to around one percent of the total issue.
The Deutsche Telekom flotation, Europe's largest-ever flotation, was five times oversubscribed and DWS said the issue was a great success with most of its customers holding on to their Telekom stock.

"Around 95 percent of our customers who bought shares in Deutsche Telekom are still Telekom shareholders," said Tessen von Heydebreck, Deutsche Bank management board member, with responsibility for private customers, told a press conference.
Telekom was also of strategic importance for the fund management group.

Christian Strenger, chairman of the board of DWS, Germany's largest fund management group, said: "Telekom has around a five percent weighting on the DAX index, and is therefore particularly important for our benchmark-oriented funds,"
"With its attractive dividend return it offers an interesting alternative to bonds, especially in the current interest rate environment," said Strenger.
Strenger said that the future progress development of the share price would depend on how the group paid down its debt and on earnings development, which would be decided by Telekom management.
DWS said it was important that the Telekom sell-off help foster a culture of long-term share ownership in Germany.

In the wake of the Telekom sell-off many German banks have introduced communications and media stocks aimed at taking up the surplus capital from those who did not get the full allocation of Telekom shares.
DWS said it was offering German investors its Telemedia fund, based on communications and media stocks, which it had been offering for some time.
